$comment: Adversarial corpus for accessibleNameSelector. Every case was MEASURED against a live webview, never reasoned about. `expect` records the behaviour of the contract as it stands; a case marked status=known-defect records what the probe DOES today together with what it SHOULD do — freezing a defect as if it were the contract is how a golden fixture stops being a judge. | 2026-08-16, quatrieme tour : trois known-defects REPARES (d-nul-only, d-lone-low, d-lone-high-mid) — leur attente est passee a ce que `shouldBe` decrivait, PUIS mesuree. d-nul-early reste tel quel avec un desaccord argumente dans son champ `note`. Aucune attente n'a ete re-derivee du comportement courant.

contract.resolution: unique = exactly one node and it is the case's own element; ambiguous = more than one, own element included; zero = no node while the element is present; none = the probe returns a null selector
contract.operators: = (whole raw value carried) | ^= (value shortened by a NUL or by the selector bound) | null

valueEncoding: Each attribute value is the INNER of a JSON string, ASCII only: read it with JSON.parse('"' + value + '"'). A run of 20+ identical characters is folded into {{c*N}} and must be expanded AFTER unescaping. No literal non-ASCII character may ever appear here — the corpus is made of characters that are invisible on screen.

attributeCases.intent: Baseline: an ordinary label composes an exact selector.
Non-ASCII letters are not a problem and must not be escaped.
A quote and a backslash used to make querySelector THROW. They must be escaped, not dropped.
Leading and trailing spaces. The displayed name trims them; the DOM does not. Composing on the display yields ZERO nodes.
A double space inside the value. Same class as above and the one that occurs in real code.
A newline in the attribute: collapsed by the display normalisation, and illegal raw in a CSS string.
A tab: same double bind as the newline.
U+00A0 is whitespace to the JS regex and an ordinary character to the DOM. The gap between the two is the defect.
U+2028 LINE SEPARATOR is in the JS \s class. Most people do not know that.
U+FEFF is in the JS \s class too. A stray BOM inside a value is enough.
U+0000 makes equality unreachable: neither the NUL nor U+FFFD matches. The cut before it keeps the element reachable by prefix.
attributeCases.note: Ambiguous by construction — the prefix is whatever precedes the NUL. The count is what makes that visible.

attributeCases.intent: U+0001, unlike the NUL, survives escaping and composes an exact match. The two control characters are NOT interchangeable.
Brackets are literal inside a quoted CSS string and must NOT be escaped.
A single quote does not close a double-quoted string. Escaping it would break the match.
Selector operators appearing INSIDE the value are inert. Guards against a naive escape pass.
CSS punctuation and a comment sequence inside the value are inert.
A complete surrogate pair well inside the bound must be left alone.

REGRESSION GUARD, and its original purpose is now moot. It used to cut mid-pair at the 80 bound; with a selector bound of 200 its raw value fits whole. It now pins the opposite property: the DISPLAY bound must not shorten the selector. Expecting '=' here is what fails if anyone composes on the display value again.
A ZWJ emoji sequence: several pairs plus joiners, none of them whitespace.
Right-to-left text plus U+200F. Visually scrambled, mechanically ordinary.
U+00AD is invisible and is NOT whitespace. It must survive into the selector.
Exactly the display bound. Pins that the display boundary has no effect on the operator.
One past the display bound. Used to produce a prefix that swallowed c-exactly80; must now be an exact match of its own.
10000 characters. Pins that the answer does not explode and that the selector bound applies.
attributeCases.note: Overlaps d-len201; this is the case to drop first if the fixture must shrink.

attributeCases.intent: Whitespace-only is not a name: no name, no selector, and no fallback available.
A whitespace-only aria-label must FALL THROUGH to the title, not report an empty name.
An empty aria-label must fall through the same way.
Two elements sharing their first 80 characters. Under the old contract they produced byte-identical rows; the selector bound of 200 now separates them.
The other half of the pair above.
The bare shared prefix, present so a prefix match would visibly capture three elements if the bounds regressed.
The real value found in ona/app/src/atelier/AtelierTab.svelte:83 — double spaces around an em dash. The only in-the-wild witness of the whole class; it must never be edited to match the fixture.
The name lives in ANOTHER element, so no attribute selector over this one can carry it. Null is the honest answer.
A button whose ancestor carries the SAME aria-label. Without tag qualification the equality hits both.
One below the selector bound: exact match.
EXACTLY the selector bound: still an exact match. This is the boundary no unit test covers — a surviving mutant proved it.
One above the selector bound: prefix match.
The bound cut lands INSIDE a surrogate pair. A lone high surrogate at the edge makes the prefix resolve to zero, so the cut must step back one unit.
The cut lands just AFTER a complete pair. The step-back must NOT fire here.
Two elements sharing 200 characters and differing after. The shortened selectors are byte-identical; only the reported match count separates the rows.
The other half of the pair above.
A NUL in first position leaves nothing to compose. Must be null, never [attr^=""] which matches every element carrying the attribute.
A NUL in second position leaves a ONE-CHARACTER prefix. The empty guard does not fire and the selector is nearly as wide as the empty one.
attributeCases.note: ⚖ DESACCORD ASSUME avec le `shouldBe` d'origine, qui demandait un plancher de longueur. Un seuil de 8 a ete essaye puis RETIRE : il detruisait des selecteurs legitimes (`[title^="avant"]` atteint exactement un element) pour attraper un cas degenere, et il inventait un nombre magique que rien ne mesurait. Surtout il aurait ete une rustine : `[aria-label="Fermer onglet"]` attrape deux elements a longueur PLEINE, donc la largeur n'a jamais ete une propriete des prefixes courts. La largeur est desormais RAPPORTEE (`accessibleNameSelectorMatches` vaut 25 ici) et lue avant d'agir.

attributes.title: a beaucoup de titres commencent ainsi

attributeCases.intent: A plausible title starting with the same letter as d-nul-early. Present so the width of that one-character prefix is visible rather than theoretical.
A lone high surrogate immediately followed by a NUL: the NUL cut must run first, then the surrogate step-back on the result.

An aria-label holding nothing but a NUL. The NUL is neither JS whitespace nor trimmed, so it is accepted as a name and MASKS the valid title behind it. ⭐ REPARE 2026-08-16 : `bounded` rejette desormais une valeur sans substance composable (NUL, surrogate isole, controle seul), donc la marche W3C atteint le `title`.
A newline followed by HEX DIGITS. The hex escape must be closed by a space or CSS eats the following letters as more digits.
A newline followed by a SPACE. CSS consumes at most one whitespace as the escape terminator, so the literal space must survive.
A newline followed by TWO spaces, to pin that only one is consumed.
A control character in last position.
A control character in first position.
A carriage return. The CSS preprocessor rewrites a RAW one, so it must arrive escaped.
CR immediately followed by LF: two escapes in a row, and a sequence the preprocessor collapses when raw.
A form feed, also rewritten by the preprocessor when raw.
A vertical tab, whose hex escape is \b and reads like a different escape entirely.
U+007F, the one escaped character outside the C0 range.
Three consecutive control characters, so consecutive escapes are exercised.
U+0085 is a C1 control that the escape does NOT cover. Pins that it does not need to: CSS carries it literally.
U+009F, the far end of the C1 range, same point.

A lone LOW surrogate in first position. The step-back only inspects the last character and only for a HIGH surrogate, so this passes straight through. ⭐ REPARE 2026-08-16 : `composablePrefix` s'arrete au PREMIER caractere non composable ou qu'il soit. Ici le surrogate isole est en tete, donc rien n'est composable et le selecteur est `null` — refus assume, plus un zero silencieux.

A lone HIGH surrogate in the MIDDLE of the value — not at the cut, so the step-back never sees it. ⭐ REPARE 2026-08-16 : la portion AVANT le surrogate isole reste utilisable, donc un prefixe qui resout.
attributeCases.note: ⚖ ATTENTE CORRIGEE PAR RAISONNEMENT, pas re-derivee du comportement. Elle disait `unique` : c'etait FAUX quand je l'ai ecrite. La valeur est 'ab' + surrogate isole, donc la portion composable fait DEUX caracteres, et `[title^="ab"]` ne peut pas etre unique dans une page de 71 elements — aucune mesure n'etait necessaire pour le savoir. ⇒ C'est le COUT ASSUME de l'absence de plancher de longueur (voir `d-nul-early`) : le selecteur elargit au lieu de rendre zero. Le progres est reel — 3 matches VISIBLES via `accessibleNameSelectorMatches` valent mieux que 0 silencieux — mais ce n'est pas une prise unique, et l'ecrire serait mentir.

attributeCases.intent: An aria-label holding a single NBSP falls through to the title correctly, because NBSP IS in the JS whitespace class. The contrast with d-nul-only is the whole point: the fallback turns on one character.

wrapperCases.intent: A div[role=button] carrying the same aria-label as the button it wraps. Without tag qualification a plain equality hits both; with it, each reaches only itself.
wrapperCases.build: wrap c-nested-child in <div id="c-nested-parent" role="button" aria-label="Zone de reglages">

parsedCases.intent: A character reference: the DOM holds the DECODED value, and the selector must carry the decoded form too.
A quote arriving through a character reference rather than through setAttribute.
A newline the parser produces. Pins that the escape path is reached from the parser, not only from JS.
Proves the HTML parser turns a NUL reference into U+FFFD, so the NUL path is unreachable from markup and only JS can produce it. This is what bounds how much the NUL cases matter.
The most ordinary way a NBSP enters a real page.
A literal newline inside an attribute in the SOURCE — how a wrapped attribute reaches the DOM in real templates.
An uppercase attribute NAME in the source. HTML lowercases it on both sides, so the hardcoded lowercase name in the composed selector is safe.
An SVG anchor picked up by the map's a[href] clause. The tag must be OMITTED: SVG tag names are case-sensitive in selectors.

parsedCases.html: <svg width="20" height="20"><rect id="e-svg-rect" role="button" aria-label="rect svg" width="10" height="10"/></svg>
parsedCases.intent: An SVG shape reached through [role=button]. Same rule, and it also proves aria-label works across the namespace boundary.
